basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: An address is a reference to a place, independent of who lives or works there.
It differs from a parcel, building or premises; one site can have several addresses.
Positions always carry a coordinate reference system and, for dynamic systems, an epoch.
Civic, postal and emergency address classes can disagree for the same site.

may: Validate and parse addresses against authority data.
Geocode and reverse geocode with stated accuracy.
Render a postal address for a destination country.
mustNot: Publish positions with more precision than their accuracy.
Undo safety coarsening of a position.
Delete retired addresses that may still be referenced.
Use a postal address for emergency dispatch without checking its class.
Link addresses to occupants beyond the declared purpose.
requiresHuman: Assigning or retiring an official address.
Releasing precise locations of protected persons or sites.

considerations: Home addresses reveal where people live; exposure can endanger victims of violence.
Wrong emergency addresses delay help in life-threatening situations.
People without formal addresses are excluded from services.

items: An address is recognised by its components, an authority, and a lifecycle status.
Confused with a coordinate, a building, a mailbox, and an informal place name.
Emergency dispatch to the wrong location.
Coordinate errors from mixed reference systems.
UPU S42 international postal address components.
